origin: Own exact three-example, two-feature classification study, designed to diagnose optimizer-dependent implicit bias rather than empirical generalization performance. Feature/label values are constructed inputs, all model parameters are dimensionless and there is no intercept. The small data size permits an exact global phase diagram and a delicate degenerate-asymptotic analysis; scientific difficulty is not dataset size.
model_and_loss: For physical-coordinate weightsw=(w1,w2), logits arew dotx and L(w)=sum_i log[1+exp(-y_i*w dotx_i)], an UNAVERAGED sum. There is no regularizer, intercept, stochastic sampling or finite-step optimizer. Each run startsw(0)=(0,0). The prescribed continuous gradient flow is dw/dt=-Q_q grad_w L, Q_q=diag(q,1),q>0. The supplied q panel uses EXACT rational fractions; numerical tool decimals approximate those exact values only for finite-time computation. This is Euclidean flow after the linear parameterizationw=diag(sqrt(q),1)*theta. The physical feature coordinates and physical test points remain fixed whenq changes; transforming them inconsistently changes the experiment.
global_implicit_direction: Derive the signed-margin feature rowsz_i=y_i*x_i and verify strict separability. Establish the optimizer-metric hard-margin variational problem governing the leading flow direction, with constraintsz_i dotwhat>=1 and objective0.5*what^T Q_q^-1 what. Justify the logistic-tail/max-margin connection for THIS positive-metric continuous flow, and do not substitute a finite L2-regularized logistic fit or finite-step intercept model. Derive the ENTIREq>0piecewise solution and all transitionq values by full primal/dual KKT feasibility, including both boundary values. Distinguish tight margin constraints from those with a strictly positive dual multiplier. Retain actual complete registered KKT linear-system solutions at every requestedq, plus full registered matrix products verifying stationarity and margins. Strict convexity must establish global uniqueness; a numerical grid or a candidate active set alone does not.
dual_convention: Use multipliersalpha_i>=0 forconstraints1-z_i dotwhat<=0, soQ_q^-1 what=sum_i alpha_i*z_i. Report all threealpha_i in exampleID order1,2,3. ID sets are unordered subsets of the PUBLIC IDs1,2,3; tightness and strict positivity are exact mathematical properties, not solver tolerance labels.
degenerate_learning_asymptotics: For each q in the panel derive the two leading scales w(t)=what(q)*log(t)+eta(q)*log(log(t))+O(1) as t tends to infinity. Determine eta, including the transition cases where a tight constraint has zero dual weight. Justify any loglog correction from the actual flow and its residual/transverse dynamics or an applicable theorem with its conditions; do not assume an O(1) residual at a degenerate boundary because generic data have one. A three-time regression is not an asymptotic proof. Constants inside the leading log differ under changes of time normalization and initialization, so retain the prescribed loss sum and flow.
finite_flow_verification: Independently integrate the exact coupled flow from0and report both weights and the NATURAL LOGARITHM of the UNAVERAGED summed logistic loss at tau=log(1+t) equal10,30,80 for eachq. Compute log(sum_i log[1+exp(-z_i dotw)]), not the sum of logarithms of individual losses and not the log of an averaged loss. Log reporting resolves the exponentially small positive loss without an absolute-tolerance zero. The change of variables means t=exp(tau)-1; integrate d w/d tau=exp(tau)*d w/dt, with actual stable logistic-tail arithmetic, convergence/refinement and all requested components retained. These trajectories verify the asymptotic mechanism but do not define its coefficients. Do not silently replace log(t) by t or interpret finite-tau residuals as the exact eta limit.
OOD_boundary_diagnostic: This part asks model LOGITS, not correctness against unavailable labels. At q=2/3use the fixed physical pointx=(1,-2/3);at q=3/2usex=(1,-3/2). For each, derive lim[w(t) dotx/log(log(t))]. Their leading what dotx can vanish while the unnormalized logit still diverges. Separately at q=0.5usex=(1,-2/3),and at q=2usex=(1,-3/2); derive each finite limiting unnormalized logit from the exact positive-dual regime residual equations and prescribed loss convention. Explain why normalized-direction agreement on a boundary does not settle logistic probability calibration there. No claimed test accuracy or causal effect follows without labels.

interpretation_proposals.A: A linear reparameterization can change the implicit norm and classifier direction while leaving the loss infimum unchanged.
interpretation_proposals.B: Every tight hard-margin constraint necessarily has a positive KKT multiplier.
interpretation_proposals.C: A degenerate support constraint can produce a loglog-time correction absent in a generic bounded-residual approximation.
interpretation_proposals.D: A zero leading normalized test margin forces the unnormalized test logit to converge tozero.
interpretation_proposals.E: Exact active-set feasibility and strict convexity establish a global margin solution beyond a finiteq grid.
interpretation_proposals.F: A regularized finite logistic estimator is automatically the same scientific object as unregularized infinite-time flow.
interpretation_proposals.G: Prediction direction, unnormalized logits and probability calibration are distinct asymptotic questions.
interpretation_proposals.H: Three unlabeled diagnostic points establish scientific generalization accuracy for a population.

Preserve source rows and labels, the correct metric/loss/time conventions, complete refined coupled integrations and controlled boundary-asymptotic derivations in the trajectory. Do not apply probability normalization to weight, multiplier or logit lists.
